extracted.intended_audience: joint force commanders, combatant command planners, public affairs officers (PAOs), and joint staff planners
extracted.subtask_short: public affairs planning for joint operations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, resourcing, coordinating, and executing public affairs (PA) activities during joint military operations, including development of PAG/PPAG and Annex F. Emphasizes OPSEC, media access, imagery handling, communications, personnel, and integration with other staff functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Affairs Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: PA activities are divided into public information, command information, and community engagement supported by planning and analysis and assessment throughout the course of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public information: provide information of a military nature consistent with security and DOD principles; Command information: communications directed to internal audiences (e.g., families, unit personnel); Community engagement: collaborative work with local groups/NGOs/OGAs to support civil-military operations. Use appropriate dissemination capabilities (including Internet) for each function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accurate and timely information
rubrics_metrics.description: PA shall provide accurate and timely information about US military operations and objectives to external (domestic and international) and DOD internal audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include briefings, statements, interviews, responses to queries, arranging access to units, and providing equipment/transportation/communications to media. Timeliness includes near-real-time and live transmission when required, balanced with security considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support media coverage and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Support US and international media coverage of US military operations by ensuring media have access to information they need to report on operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct briefings, issue statements, arrange interviews, provide access to operational units, include media on deploying platforms where appropriate, provide transportation and communications support, and plan for embedding/media pools while not compromising OPSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to understanding and deterrence
rubrics_metrics.description: PA should contribute to global understanding and deterrence by making audiences aware of US resolve, capabilities, and intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use themes, messages, and imagery proactively to inform public and international audiences about objectives and capabilities to shape strategic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate and counter adversary misinformation/disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigate and counter adversary disinformation (propaganda) and misinformation by actively using accurate and timely public information and imagery to preempt and respond to inaccurate information and deception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct media analysis and assessment to identify adversary narratives; use facts, imagery, and timely releases to preempt misleading narratives; coordinate with IO and MISO where appropriate while avoiding counterproductive overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate PA into all operational phases
rubrics_metrics.description: PA should be incorporated in every phase of operations and in the planning process from earliest predeployment stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA planners participate throughout JOPP, provide input to mission statements, COA development, wargaming, and plan/order development. Early planning should identify resource requirements, access plans for media, and procedures that allow reasonable access without compromising mission or OPSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Affairs Guidance (PAG/PPAG) content and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs guidance (PAG) and proposed PAG (PPAG) support public discussion of defense issues and serve as source documents when responding to media and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAG/PPAG should ensure information conforms to policy and OPSEC/privacy requirements and should address PA policy, contingency statements, levels of authority for release/classification, declassification guidance, themes, messages, talking points, and responses to anticipated media questions. Develop and timely disseminate PAG to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex F (Public Affairs) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Annex F of an OPORD should address all PA-related transportation, communications, billeting, equipment, and personnel resources required to support the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex F should capture detailed planning considerations (e.g., exercises, media access, visual information, MOCs, embedding/media pools, intelligence support, technology support, command information, AFRTS, communications guidance, internet-based products/releases) and complement but not replace PPAG forwarded to OASD(PA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and MOC requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate facilities with appropriate infrastructure for PA and media operations centers (MOCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities may require staff and media work areas, equipment storage, imaging facilities, access to helicopter landing zones, vehicle parking, AFRTS broadcast/transmission facilities, billeting and messing, and work areas for community engagement and command information missions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel: deployability and augmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: PA personnel and equipment should be deployable and provided on a dedicated basis; contingency planning must address rapid expansion/augmentation of PA personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific skills and capabilities required; reflect skill sets in OPLANs/OPORDs RFFs; use AC/RC PA units and individual augmentees; pre-identify billets and match individuals to requirements; prioritize augmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment identification and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs should identify necessary equipment and seek standardization to facilitate interoperability and minimize training requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify hardware, software, digital imaging, TV monitors, video/digital recorders, reception capability, and AFRTS deployable distribution packages (over air radio/TV, cable, L-Band). Identify broadcast frequencies via communications directorate and plan maintenance/service support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications capacity and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide bandwidth priority and appropriate communications capabilities to support timely transmission of PA and VI products (including large files and live streaming) and unfiltered Internet access for information/imagery release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate bandwidth for classified and unclassified products (files >250 MB; streaming at ~5 Mbps surge), provide LAN and unclassified/classified web-based sites, ensure mix of tactical and strategic comms (phones, radios, satellite uplinks) to support PA operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation and mobility support
rubrics_metrics.description: PA mobility should match that of other operational forces; provide transportation assets to move PA personnel, media, and information products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transportation package may include vehicles with drivers/communications, force protection escorts, fixed- and rotary-wing aircraft for media, and surface/air transport for imagery/products. Prioritize movement of PA assets in logistics planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media operations centers (MOC) establishment and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish MOCs as appropriate to provide timely public and command information products and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOCs (aka joint information bureau, combined press information center) should be coordinated with ASD(PA), provide direct PA support and oversight to subordinate JFCs and be prepared to coordinate participation in multinational MOCs; designate MOC director and JTF PAO as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery acquisition, review, and release
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagery requirements must be identified and synchronized with imagery-producing capabilities; imagery that supports joint operations should be forwarded to DIMOC and reviewed for security concerns and cleared for public release at the lowest appropriate level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate COMCAM/VI requirements, identify COMCAM imagery needs in operational planning, assign COMCAM liaison teams, plan for in-theater declassification and delegation of in-theater release to meet time-sensitive media requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPSEC integration and balance with release
rubrics_metrics.description: PA releases must be aware of and governed by OPSEC considerations to protect critical information associated with sensitive operations and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA should provide assessments of possible effects of media coverage, work with OPSEC planners to develop guidelines, participate in OPSEC surveys and security reviews, and balance tension between OPSEC and need to release information—temporary transmission delays may be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with IO, MISO, MILDEC, CNO/EW and other functions
rubrics_metrics.description: PA must coordinate and deconflict activities with Information Operations (IO), Military Information Support Operations (MISO), Military Deception (MILDEC), Computer Network Operations (CNO), and Electronic Warfare (EW).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deconflict planning to avoid PA and MISO countering each other; safeguard deception plans when coordinating with MILDEC; coordinate PA/CNO/EW activities to avoid conflicts; ensure PA and IO coordination consistent with DOD principles, policy, legal limits, and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA participation in JOPP steps
rubrics_metrics.description: PA actions are required across the Joint Operation Planning Process (JOPP) including initiation, mission analysis, COA development, wargaming, COA comparison, COA approval, and plan/order development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA should begin operational environment analysis, participate in JIPOE, identify intelligence requirements, specify PA tasks, develop PA facts/assumptions/estimates, conduct force structure analysis, provide PA input to mission statements, participate in COA wargaming and provide PA input to approved COAs, and develop Annex F and submit PPAG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission analysis: media environment and PA tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: During mission analysis, PA planners develop situational understanding of the operational environment including media infrastructure, capability and bias, social and cultural characteristics, and identify specified, implied, and essential PA tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop initial PA staff estimates, identify imagery/AFRTS/DOD Media Pool needs, develop PA facts and assumptions, identify intelligence requirements for PA, and participate in cross-functional staff organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and exercises for PA readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: PA personnel and appropriate staff members should be trained in JOPP and PA tasks; PA training objectives should be included in command exercise objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise PA processes with attention to coordination with operational staff, resourcing PA functions, OPSEC concerns, and use universal joint tasks to drive training; include scenarios designed to assess PA readiness and identification/training of augmentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and feedback of PA activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders must evaluate communication activities and associated results; PAOs should use all feedback sources to determine effectiveness and inform future planning and strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results and assessments should inform plan and strategy development, refine PA requirements, and feed into measures of effectiveness in Annex Y (SC) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to families, command information programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan command information programs to support deployed forces, their home stations, and family members to dispel rumors and anxieties and to increase understanding of the joint force’s missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish ground rules to release information and imagery to civilian media; information approved for media release should also be provided to command information staff; consider effects on morale and focus of service members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting and other logistical support
rubrics_metrics.description: PA staff should have access to contracting support and government purchase card authority to obtain goods and services not available within the joint force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include contracts for publication of command information products, services and equipment for media analysis/assessment, maintenance/service contracts for sustainability, and contracted translation services.
